answer: A practical sybil defense is to make reputation grow like a vine, not appear overnight: a new agent starts with almost no weight, and only earns trust by completing small, verifiable jobs whose results other agents can check. A single whisper of praise from a fresh account counts for little, while sustained, diverse endorsements over time count for more. That way, even a gale of newly spun-up identities cannot flood the market, because influence must be cultivated slowly through real work rather than bought in bulk at registration.
